title: Harmonize proxy backpressure with OpenAI-compat structured-output quotas and reduce stream jitter
author: Sofia Mendez
description:
Context: Customers saw intermittent stream jitter and truncated structured outputs when routing to OpenAI-compat endpoints during brief spike conditions. Investigation showed the gateway's per-connection write buffer and the route-level in-flight byte accounting were not aligned with the OpenAI compatibility layer's expectations for function/tool call handshake fragments. This caused small fragments (fncall/openai-compat structured chunks) to be re-ordered or dropped under proxy backpressure, and also allowed oversized structured fields to bypass per-route soft-quotas during streaming.

Goal: Make proxy backpressure behavior deterministic for structured outputs and tool/function calls, enforce a per-route "structured-output soft quota" during streaming, and add an edge-level jitter damping window to reduce reorder under transient congestion. Keep changes minimally invasive and reversible.

What this PR does (summary): 1) Introduces a per-route in-flight byte window (route_inflight_window_bytes) that the gateway enforces in writer paths; the value is conservative by default and configurable per route. 2) Adds a structured_output_quota soft-check that triggers backpressure earlier for responses that contain structured output markers or function-call fragments to avoid mid-stream truncation. 3) Implements a short jitter_damping_timer (10-40ms adaptive) that coalesces very small successive fragments from upstream to reduce re-order risk when the proxy applies backpressure. 4) Adds a handshake fencing check for fncall/toolcall shards: a short-lived ack token is required to accept a follow-up shard as part of the same logical function/tool call (helps avoid cross-request contamination under concurrency). 5) Exposes new route-level diagnostics to Redwood Console (small telemetry keys) and a gating feature flag (gateway.backpressure.harmonize) to allow canary rollout.

Why this approach: Prior fixes changed buffer sizes which reduced throughput or increased latency; instead, we align per-route accounting with structured-output semantics so the gateway pressures the upstream before protocol-level fragments become partial. The jitter damping coalescer uses a very small adaptive timer to avoid adding measurable latency in normal traffic but absorbs pathological microbursts that previously caused re-order. The handshake fencing prevents accidental mix of fncall shards across concurrently routed requests when the proxy re-queues fragments due to backpressure.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add route_inflight_window_bytes config and default; 
- [x] Implement structured_output_quota soft-check; 
- [x] Add jitter_damping_timer coalescer in proxy writer; 
- [x] Add handshake fencing token for fncall/toolcall shards; 
- [x] Add console telemetry keys and docs snippet; 
- [x] Backwards-compatible feature flag gating; 
- [x] Unit tests for quota and handshake fencing; 
- [x] E2E streaming integration test (flake fixed after retry); 
- [x] Update changelog/release notes entry.

Commits (high-level):
- 77412a: add route-level inflight accounting and config plumbing
- 77412b: implement structured_output_quota checks in proxy writer path
- 77412c: jitter coalescer + adaptive timer implementation and tuning heuristics
- 77412d: handshake fencing token generation and validation for fncall shards
- 77412e: expose telemetry metrics + console doc update + test fixes

Files (changed, high-level):
- gateway/proxy/writer.go (core changes: inflight accounting, coalescer insertion)
- gateway/config/routes.go (route_inflight_window_bytes, structured_output_quota fields)
- gateway/proxy/handshake.go (handshake fencing token logic)
- gateway/compat/openai/stream_adapter.go (compat layer detects structured markers and tags stream frames)
- console/telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml (add route.gateway.structured_quota.{used,throttles})
- docs/source/gateway/streaming.md (notes on new soft quota and feature flag)
- test/integration/streaming_jitter_test.go (e2e harness and flaky-case fixes)

Small illustrative snippet (proxy writer change): "if route.InflightBytes+frame.Size() > route.InflightWindowBytes { applyBackpressure(); return enqueueForDrain(frame) } else { writeImmediate(frame) }" — the actual code includes atomic counters and a small lease to avoid thundering-writes.

Review timeline and conversation (condensed):
- Evan Park (review): "Overall solid. A couple of notes: we should be conservative with the default inflight window and ensure the telemetry tags are low-cardinality. Also, add a metric for rejected-shards so ops can triage."
- Sofia (author): "Addressed: lowered default inflight to 64KB for public routes, added rejected_shards counter, ensured telemetry uses route id + environment only."
- Riley Chen (review): "The handshake token logic looks good, but we need to ensure it doesn't hold memory in the proxy for long-lived streams. Can we TTL aggressively and use a small LRU?"
- Sofia: "Implemented TTL + LRU eviction; added unit test for eviction edge case."
- Priya Kapoor (approver): "Tests looked stable after the second CI run. Approving for canary rollout."

CI summary: Initial CI run failed one streaming integration (timing-sensitive) test. Root cause: the test harness expected strictly byte-aligned frames; adjusted harness to be tolerant of coalesced fragments and re-ran. Second run: all checks passed. Key checks: unit (pass), integration/streaming (pass), linters (pass), load smoke (pass).

Observability and rollout: The feature is gated behind gateway.backpressure.harmonize. We enabled the gate in Canary region A with route-level defaults reduced to be extra conservative; telemetry shows a 72% reduction in truncated structured outputs and a 38% reduction in stream reorders for affected routes during canary window. No customer-facing incidents were observed.

Release notes: "Gateway: improve streaming stability for structured outputs and function/tool calls by adding per-route inflight accounting, structured-output soft quotas, and jitter damping. Rollout is gated; enable via gateway.backpressure.harmonize."

notes_for_ops: Gate default is off in main; enable per-cluster or per-route with gateway.backpressure.harmonize. Watch metrics route.gateway.structured_quota.throttles and route.gateway.rejected_shards for regressions.
post_merge_actions: 1) Enable gate in canary region for 48h, 2) monitor telemetry and escalate if rejected_shards > 0.5% of stream traffic, 3) roll to other regions if stable.
